subject: Inference telemetry gating & onshore carveout — evidence and timeline
messages:
From: Blueleaf Health Security <security@blueleaf.health>

Subject: SSQ follow-up: telemetry exports, PII gating, onshore carveout artifacts

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our security team had a follow-up after reviewing the initial SSQ — a few clarifications before we move to procurement:

1) We need an annotated dataflow diagram that shows where inference telemetry (prompt/response traces, latency metrics, sampling telemetry) is collected, what elements are treated as PII, and which components are subject to the onshore carveout (data that must remain or be processed only in US regions). A simple visual + brief legend will suffice.

2) Confirm which telemetry fields are persisted vs transient (KV caches, request traces, anonymized metrics). If you persist any request/response content, we need retention windows and redaction rules.

3) Subprocessor gating: we require a single-page summary that lists the subprocessors involved in telemetry export (analytics, observability), whether they are subject to SOC 2, and the process for getting onshore-only exceptions approved.

4) KMS and key custody: high-level attestation that customer data used for inference telemetry can be encrypted with customer-managed keys or, if not, a documented explanation of key custody and rotation cadence.

Can you provide these artifacts as attachments or Drive links? Ideally by end of week (COB Fri local). We may have follow-up once we review.

Attachment: blueleaf_ssq_v2.pdf (SSQ with specific line items called out)

Appreciate it —
Carter Lin
Procurement / Blueleaf Health

Kimberly — initial drafts attached / links below. Per the split:

1) Annotated dataflow: redwood_annotated_dataflow_v1.svg (attached) and a one-page legend that maps fields to classification. Key callouts:
  - \"user_input\" and \"user_metadata.email\" are classified as PII (we mark them in red).
  - Model telemetry (latency, token counts, anonymized error traces) is non-PII and stored as aggregated metrics for 90 days by default.
  - Request/response bodies are not persisted by default except for customer opt-in debug logs; opt-in logs are retained 30 days and redacted of email-like patterns before storage.

2) Export paths: diagram shows telemetry forwarded to our analytics subproc (Observlytics Inc.) for aggregation; that path is blocked under onshore carveout unless explicit carveout approval is in place.

3) Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-ExampleShare/annotated-dataflow (diagram + legend + sample policy)

4) Evidence we can include: Observlytics SOC 2 summary (we have an executed attestation on file), and the redaction policy doc (onshore-carveout-runbook.pdf).

I'll redact a synthetic sample trace to show how redaction runs (no real PII). Connor — do you want me to bundle those artifacts into a single zip for sending, or do you prefer individual links?

Carter / Blueleaf Security —

Thanks for the checklist. Please find the requested artifacts below and a short summary for each ask. If you'd like a quick walkthrough, we can schedule a 30-minute call.

Artifacts provided (attached + Drive):
- Annotated dataflow diagram (redwood_annotated_dataflow_v1.svg) — shows ingestion, inference proxy, telemetry aggregator, and export paths. Legend indicates PII fields (user identifiers, email).
- Onshore carveout runbook (onshore-carveout-runbook.pdf) — describes routing rules that prevent telemetry export to external analytics subprocessors unless an approved carveout is in place. Includes operational steps and required approvals.
- KMS attestation summary (kms-attestation-summary.pdf) — describes key custody model. For telemetry data we currently support envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys; for customers that require CMKs we have a roadmap and short-term mitigations described in the attestation.
- Observlytics SOC excerpt (provided as part of subproc summary).

Summary answers to your bullets:
1) Telemetry / PII: Fields classified as PII are identified on the diagram. Default retention: aggregated metrics = 90 days; opt-in debug traces (redacted) = 30 days. No live customer PII is shared with analytics subprocessors unless an onshore carveout is approved.
2) Persistence vs transient: KV caches are transient per-request (evicted after session end); traces are either aggregated or opt-in. We have an automated redaction pipeline that removes email patterns and SSNs from opt-in traces before storage.
3) Subprocessor gating & SOC 2: Observlytics Inc. (analytics) and TelemetryHub (ingest queue) are the two main subprocessors involved. Both have SOC 2 attestations on file; our subproc gating process is documented in the runbook. For onshore carveouts, we require a signed exception and ask that you approve the carveout scope via procurement route.
4) KMS: See attached attestation. We currently use Redwood-managed keys for telemetry; customers requiring CMKs are handled as an enterprise offering with a short onboarding timeline (~4–6 weeks).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-ExampleShare/annotated-dataflow
HubSpot reference: BL-4723

If you want, we can redact a synthetic trace and include a short video walkthrough. Please let us know the best time for a 30-minute call next week.

Best —
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference
